messages:
maria: Heads-up — after the role/permission propagation refactor we rolled yesterday we're seeing a case where a workspace claim from org-B was accepted as valid for an org-A project during a KMS key rotation. Not exploitable widely (so far) but it allowed a single request from tenant-B to access a dataset owned by tenant-A. :eyes:

deploy-bot: alert: policy-eval anomaly detected for request-id=8f3a2c. https://internal.incidents/redwood/alerts/8f3a2c — env:prod — triggered at 2025-11-03T02:11:22Z

samir: Can you paste minimal repro steps + the exact logs? I want to see the claim/issuer and KMS assertion mapping.

maria: Repro steps quick: 1) rotate KMS key for org-A (we did at 02:10 UTC) 2) immediately send request signed with old claim from org-B that previously had been denied 3) membership service returned cached membership -> policy eval returned OK. Logs: ```[2025-11-03T02:11:23Z] request=8f3a2c svc=policy-eval user_claim={iss: "org-b", sub: "user:123"} project=org-a/project-77 eval_result=ALLOW reason="membership_cache_hit" membership_rev=137 cache_ttl=300s ```

chris: Wait — membership_cache_hit? TTL is 5m right? If KMS rotated, we should have invalidated assertions that depend on key alias. Did the KMS rotation publish an event to key-change topic?

maria: KMS rotation did publish: ``EVENT: kms.rotate key=org-a-main at 2025-11-03T02:10:55Z``. membership service log right after rotation: ```[2025-11-03T02:10:59Z] svc=membership-cache key_lookup=stale -> returning cached membership rev=137``` So there is a 4s gap where membership-cache still served entries. It looks like our membership cache doesn't subscribe to KMS key changes.

kyle: This smells like a race between kms-assertor and membership-cache on claim binding. The refactor changed where we stamp `project_claim_revision` and we dropped an explicit invalidation call in kms-rotate handler. We need either: 1) invalidate membership cache on key rotation, or 2) make policy-eval check claim_revision monotonic against KMS artifact version. Quick mitigation = invalidate on rotation and emergency deploy.

samir: Can we run a quick membership query for that user now and show the claim_revision fields? curl example: ```curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" "https://membership.internal/v1/projects/org-a/users/user:123" | jq .```

maria: Output now after manual invalidate: ```{ "user":"user:123", "memberships":[], "project_claim_revision": 0, "last_seen": "2025-11-03T02:12:40Z" }``` Previously it showed membership to org-a with rev=137. We forced a cache flush and the membership service correctly dropped the stale membership.

chris: OK. Short term: force invalidate caches for recent KMS rotates (org-a) and create an emergency canary release that adds explicit invalidation in the rotate handler. Long term: add revision binding to policy-eval so cache hits still verify kms-assertor version.

kyle: I'm opening the emergency PR to add cache invalidation and a defensive check. Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/membership-service/pull/4523 (WIP) — patch adds listeners on key-change topic and forces membership_cache.invalidate(namespace) and adds policy-eval fallback check `if membership_rev < kms_claim_rev -> deny and enqueue revalidate`.

ops-oncall: acked :lock: — I've paged infra to run the invalidate for org-a and queued the hotfix rollout to staging then canary-prod. ETA 25m.

maria: Thanks. I'll keep monitoring logs for any other cross-tenant evals and start a short postmortem doc (link: https://playbooks.redwood/security/postmortems/2025-11-kms-cache-race). For now mitigation = invalidate caches + hotfix.

chris: Also add a unit test for the refactor that simulates rotate+immediate-eval so we don't regress.

kyle: will add tests to PR.

maria: Good. If anyone sees other requests with request-id prefix 8f3a2c* please paste here. :mag:
